events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
This is a safety-flagged case (dispute type: safety), and the trace settles that no automatic ruling applies [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The rider's complaint alleges the driver threatened to lock her in when she asked to get out, and the in-app chat corroborates the exchange: at 17:09 the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here" [F3], and at 17:10 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4]. The driver's post-trip statement confirms he "told her to sit down" and "drove on" [F6]. Under SAFE-1, a threat or intimidation directed at the other party requires escalation rather than an automatic ruling; the remedy is a human review, not a refund decision [F4][SAFE-1].

The safety screen also touches SAFE-2 to the extent the conduct — refusing to stop while the rider wished to exit — is an allegation about the manner of driving and the rider's safety in the vehicle; a human reviewer should determine whether it amounts to a dangerous-conduct allegation. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages) [F5], so there is no evidence gap on the messages themselves; no refund is computed because the trace bars any automatic outcome and escalate carries no amount [F1][F2][RD-2].

Separately, the route facts show no deviation worth any fare adjustment even if the fare were in issue: actual distance 15.4 km is 0.1 km under the 15.5 km optimal route [F1], and the $32.86 fare is a fixed RydeX quote unaffected by distance [F1][F2][RD-2]. That is why the rider's own requested outcome (no_action) cannot be granted here: the safety allegation must be screened by a person before the fare is final. The profiles (rider 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 d [F7]; driver 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 d [F8]) are not used to decide anything; they are recorded only for the reviewer's context, and no account flag is warranted on these facts [RD-6].

Summary for the human reviewer: on 17:08–17:31 RydeX Clarke Quay → Bedok Mall, the rider asked to be let out mid-trip [F3] and the driver responded with a threat to lock the doors [F4], later writing that he told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on [F6]. Disputed: whether the doors were locked, whether the rider was prevented from exiting, and the driver's tone/intent. Check: the full chat export and GPS/timeline for the moment of the exchange, the vehicle's central-lock status if retrievable, and any prior safety reports on either account.
